page: Amazon Web Services t9g.small is an entry-level burstable instance designed for lightweight computing tasks. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance runs on custom AWS silicon built on the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. It provides two dedicated physical CPU cores clocked at 3.3 GHz with one thread per core, providing direct physical core allocation without simultaneous multithreading contention.

Hardware specifications allocate 2.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The t9g.small does not bundle local instance storage, requiring remote network storage volumes for persistence and operating system installations. It contains no GPU acceleration hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is designated at 0 Gbps, utilizing burst capabilities for transient network interactions.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the Arm-based core configuration delivers a cost-effective profile for low-utilization tasks. The modest 2.0 GB memory ceiling and reliance on external storage present clear tradeoffs for data-intensive or persistent I/O workloads. As a result, the instance is suited for lightweight microservices, small background workers, continuous integration agents, and development or testing environments.
